name: Imtiaz Mashrafee
lede: I build AI systems and test what they do when inputs go wrong.

projects.question: How do you stop a car being overbooked?
projects.fails: Each request for seats looks fine on its own, so a car can end up with more riders than seats.
projects.catches: At the moment a driver accepts, it counts the seats taken across the whole car, not per group.
projects.survives: Without the check a 3-seat car held 5 riders; with it, 3 of 3. Recorded against a stand-in (mock) database.
projects.limit: Two accepts at the same moment can both pass.

projects.question: When should an AI not start writing?
projects.fails: A single prompt writes a confident email even when the request is vague or missing facts.
projects.catches: Ordinary code checks the request first, then a model judges whether there is enough to write from.
projects.survives: On 10 recorded scenarios: 4.7 of 5, against 4.2 for a single prompt. One run; scoring model unrecorded.
projects.limit: For one unclear request it still wrote an email when it should have asked.

projects.question: When should an AI trust its first answer?
projects.fails: A first draft can be too short, drift off the question or stop mid-thought, and nothing says so.
projects.catches: Each draft is scored with simple quality rules; below the required quality, one more attempt with tighter settings.
projects.survives: Four recorded queries: two passed first time, two tried again and still fell short. Drafts from a mock generator.
projects.limit: Repair is an attempt, not a guarantee; both repaired answers stayed below the requirement.

projects.question: What if a reading looks valid but is not?
projects.fails: Reading a photographed lab report can misread a value, and a misread can still look like a good number.
projects.catches: Only value shapes it knows are accepted; a row that does not match is left out, not guessed.
projects.survives: Two recorded misreads: one is caught and its row left out; the other looks valid and is kept.
projects.limit: <8.5 read in place of <0.5 looks valid, so it is kept.
